checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: A user follows 5,000 accounts. How is their feed assembled?

options.label: Fan-out on read
options.sub: query all followees at request time
options.verdict: No write amplification and always fresh — but a feed load becomes thousands of queries plus a merge sort, on the read path, for a system with a 50:1 read bias. You have optimised the rare operation.

options.label: Fan-out on write
options.verdict: Reads become a single sequential fetch of an already-built list. You pay at write time, which is 50x rarer, and that is exactly the trade the read:write ratio is telling you to make.

defend.prompt: Where does pure fan-out on write break?

options.label: An account with 100M followers makes one post 100M writes
Inactive users get timelines built that nobody reads
Celebrity posts must be merged at read time instead
Feed reads get slower as following count grows

defend.explain: Read cost is now flat regardless of following count — that is the win. The break is the celebrity tail, which is why real systems run a hybrid: push for the ordinary case, pull for the handful of accounts where fan-out is absurd.

checkpoints.title: Capacity ladder
checkpoints.prompt: Twitter's published shape: 300K read QPS against 6K write QPS.

rungs.note: 300K / 6K. This single number drives the whole design.
Make the 50x rarer operation do the work.
Under 500ms, with a tweet reaching timelines within seconds.

checkpoints.explain: A 50:1 ratio is permission to do real work on write. Invert the ratio and fan-out on write becomes the wrong answer.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.prompt: Build the read path for a user opening their feed.
checkpoints.explain: The timeline is already materialised in Redis, so a feed load is one fetch plus hydration of post bodies from Cassandra. Fanout Workers and Kafka build that timeline asynchronously on the write path — they must never appear on a read.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: Feeds load fast, but a celebrity's post takes 40 minutes to appear for everyone.
checkpoints.explain: One post to 100M followers is 100M timeline writes, and the fanout queue is now 80M deep — every ordinary user's post is stuck behind it. This is precisely the case the hybrid exists for: accounts above a follower threshold should not fan out at all, and instead be merged into the timeline at read time.

wrong.Redis timeline: 96% hit rate — reads are healthy, which is why feeds still feel fast.
wrong.Feed Service: 60ms p99. It is serving timelines correctly; they are just missing a post.
wrong.Cassandra: Post bodies are being fetched fine. The problem is which post ids made it into the timeline.
